flags.summary: The standard agreement gates its 'love it or leave it' exit on the client completing and submitting all weekly check-in forms within 30 days, and in the same clause requires the client to waive the right to initiate chargeback disputes; a lawyer reading it live rejected both.
evidence: He talks about this, if client elects the optional love it or leave it, described in section 3G, oh, that's below, okay. Client further agrees not to initiate chargeback disputes.
Yeah, this is telling me I must do certain things to complete the leave-it, and I don't want to do that.
It's all the same terms, but instead of the option to leave it, I don't have to complete it or submit all weekly check-in forms with 30 days. I don't want to be hamstrung in. I want to decide.
Yeah, but, but, but I'm a lawyer. And I, and I know how contracts work.

flags.summary: The agreement lists 'private online community with calendar for coaching calls', which on questioning turned out to mean group follow-along workouts inside the separate self-paced product, not coaching calls.
evidence: What does it mean, private online community with calendar for coaching calls?
This is because Trevor is running also what is called Primal University. It's like a Self-paced, no-coaching community. And once a week, there's a live workout that he's doing and you can join him.
So the coaching calls, I'm not really doing coaching calls, right?
This is a follow along live workout with him. That's, that's what it is.
Oh, so that's not real. That's that other thing. That's not, that's additional to you.

flags.summary: Bespoke term structure outside the price book — $1,200 for a first month followed by four interest-free instalments of $1,200 — with a referral and a testimonial attached as non-monetary consideration for the terms.
evidence: So you start with the initial month... And as I said, if you're happy with that first month, and I know you will be, we split, we split. Split the remaining 4,800 into four equal installments of 1,200. No interest, like you asked.
Two small things I'd like to ask in return. Once you're a month in, send someone from your circle our way.
And once you've completed the full six months and seen the whole transformation in you, we would love to have a testimonial on your experience. Sounds fair?
I will consider it both. I won't promise that I can, but I will.

flags.summary: Rep told this prospect the six-month duration clause is merely administrative convenience, while the same clause is sold to other prospects as the substantive reason the programme cannot be shorter.
evidence: But that, but then you're going to have to go look at number three in the terms, and how the, it says, because it says up in duration program last six months. That's not necessarily true.
It's just because to have less administrative work. Yeah, that's, that's why it's.
The program is one month, with the option to continue on for six months at the price of $1,200.

flags.summary: This transcript records only a negotiation stage; the discovery call that established price, goals, health history and the one-month structure is referenced but is not present in this batch.
evidence: So look, did you go through the agreement?
But I'm willing to do it because you told me you can make the changes.
I negotiated to be able to get out after one month, but is that already standard?
No, that's what I proposed to you, that you come in for the month, and then you decide whether you want to move forward or not.

flags.summary: A prospect asked whether the coach is an AI-generated person before he would proceed, and the rep reported it as the first such challenge received.
evidence: I think you've heard this question before, but maybe you have. Is Trevor an AI-generated person on the internet?
You're the first one, actually, to ask. No, he's not AI-generated. You will talk to him.
I was like, you know, AI is getting good, but I don't know. I was like, I don't think it is, but I don't want to be had either, you know what I mean?
